searchText: Question to the Geth team: on average how long does Snap Sync take on mainnet and how long the ranges phase and the healing phase? Does snap sync get you enough data to sync a consensus client off of? No, el-data only. As for the other questions, will answer later <@869907361085685780> I just synced a couple of azure nodes (IO isn't awesome on those). Without block download (because geth can sync with ancients intact from earlier), the account/storage snap download phase took on the order of 12 hours. ``` synced=100.00% state=198.53GiB accounts=187,249,438@41.75GiB slots=765,336,548@152.83GiB codes=654,682@3.95GiB ``` The heal-phase depends heavily on 1) IO performance and 2) amount of peers. Too many peers overload the cli right now (we're working on it). For our more beefy aws-machines, we can usually do the whole thing in 12 hours. Can dig up some charts per phase for those later > I have requested left key X and right key Y, and the other node responds with only one key/value pair. Then none of those keys existed, right? So you only got the account in between. And thus the proof needs to show that indeed, following the trie downwards towards X leads to a dead end, trie-path-wise. Did I misnunderstand the question? So in case when the whole thing takes around 12h , do you know what is the ratio between the snap and the healing phase? I don't need precise numbers just some high level view. Best case a few hours. Worst case never finishes 😦 it's that worst case we're working on improving now Thanks. The charts would be very interesting. I've observed that our snap sync become less deterministic recently in terms of time.
